Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )$ for $\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{5\pi }{6}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above)?
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ),$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta ).
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ))^{2}+(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta ))^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{16{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )+144{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{16({cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )+9{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta ))}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =4{\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )+9{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
